skills.name: Design a workflow as a process map: messy prototype, then clean final map
skills.goal: Design or document a workflow by mapping it as a process map (inputs, ordered steps, decisions, stakeholders, outputs): start with a messy prototype map of the one process causing the most pain, share and iterate, then publish a clean final documentation map and keep it updated.
steps: Pick the single process that is currently causing the most trouble; skip choosing tools or depth for now.
On paper/whiteboard/sticky notes, write the steps as simple boxes in sequential order (this, then this, then this, then the final output), noting inputs, decision points, and who is involved.
Expand it into a prototype map with collaborators: add context, links to tools, screenshots, problems, and improvement ideas without worrying about looks.
Share it (photo or link), walk someone through it, collect comments, and iterate.
Produce the final documentation map: only the as-is steps in order, decisions and parallel flows from trigger to final output, with notes and clutter removed.
Move it into a shareable tool with access controls if needed, one tab per subprocess, and optionally add detailed docs/SOPs that expand each box.
Revisit the map whenever the process changes or a better way is found, and update it.

skills.name: Design an agent-run media production pipeline: map team roles to tools, encode style as a skill, improve it from feedback
skills.goal: Design an automated media workflow (shown for video editing; same pattern for automated song generation) by listing every human job in the production team, assigning each to a tool with one coordinating agent, writing the creative style into a skill file the agent reads first, and growing that skill from time-stamped human feedback after each run.
steps: List every job a human team would do to make the product (video: editor, transcriber, animator, researcher, screen editor, sound designer, finisher).
Assign each job to a tool; make the agent the coordinator/project manager that calls the others, and add a converter for any media the agent cannot perceive.
Set up the agent locally with a working folder and connect each tool/connector, then have the agent save the setup as a skill.
Open a new session and test the skill on a small piece of input, with any extra instructions.
Review the output and give specific, time-stamped feedback (look, sound, pacing, cuts); try several alternatives for one element until one fits.
Tell the agent to save what it learned into the skill, then run the next job in a fresh session with the updated skill.
Once tuned, give the full raw input, let it run unattended, then review and give final notes.
